question: What is the primary goal of quality assurance in a maternity delivery unit?

options.A: To reduce the number of staff on duty
options.B: To punish midwives who make clinical mistakes
options.C: To ensure every woman receives safe and respectful care
options.D: To increase the cost of maternity services

explanation: Quality assurance focuses on systematic checks to protect mothers and babies by promoting safe practices rather than punishing staff. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T4#BMP217_U2_T4_h1)

question: Why are frontline midwives considered central to the quality assurance process?

options.A: They write all the national health policies
options.C: They control the hospital budget and procurement
options.D: They manage normal births and spot early complications

explanation: Midwives interact directly with laboring women, placing them in the best position to deliver care and catch warning signs early. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T4#BMP217_U2_T4_h1)

question: What does a low five-minute Apgar score primarily help midwives evaluate?

options.A: The exact birth weight of the baby
options.B: The effectiveness of intrapartum care and newborn resuscitation
options.C: The mother's blood type and Rhesus factor
options.D: The length of the first stage of labor

explanation: The Apgar score checks how well the baby tolerated the birth process and responded to any help given right after delivery. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T4#BMP217_U2_T4_h2)

question: An unusually high rate of uterine rupture is recorded in a rural hospital delivery unit. What issue does this safety indicator point toward?

options.A: A high number of elective Caesarean sections
options.B: Effective infection control procedures in the theater
options.C: Possible delays in managing obstructed labor or oxytocin misuse
options.D: Excellent routine postnatal counseling for breastfeeding

explanation: Uterine rupture is strongly linked to unmonitored prolonged labor or improper use of drugs that stimulate uterine contractions. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T4#BMP217_U2_T4_h2)

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard method for gathering feedback on maternal experience?

options.A: Anonymous suggestion boxes in the postnatal ward
options.B: Secretly reading personal diaries left behind
options.D: Exit interviews conducted by neutral third parties

explanation: Patient feedback must be gathered through ethical, structured means like interviews and surveys, never by violating personal privacy. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T4#BMP217_U2_T4_h3)

question: Why is it often recommended that neutral third parties conduct exit interviews for new mothers?

options.A: Midwives do not have time to speak any local languages
options.B: Mothers may feel safer to speak honestly without fear of staff backlash
options.C: Hospital management does not care about patient opinions
options.D: Third parties are the only ones who understand medical records

explanation: Patients often fear poor treatment if they criticize the same nurses and midwives who cared for them, so neutral interviewers encourage honest answers. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T4#BMP217_U2_T4_h3)

question: What is the main question a clinical audit tries to answer in a delivery unit?

options.A: What new medical equipment can we buy from abroad?
options.B: Which midwife delivered the highest number of babies?
options.C: Are we actually doing what we know is best practice?
options.D: How much profit did the maternity ward generate this month?

explanation: Clinical audits check current actions against set standards to see where care falls short of guidelines. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T4#BMP217_U2_T4_h4)

question: What is the final step in a standard clinical audit cycle after implementing changes?

options.A: Destroying all records to maintain patient privacy
options.B: Closing the maternity unit for routine fumigation
options.C: Punishing staff members who failed the first review
options.D: Re-auditing to check if clinical practice has improved

explanation: The audit cycle is only complete when you measure again to see if your interventions fixed the problem. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T4#BMP217_U2_T4_h4)

question: What makes a quality improvement strategy effective after reviewing poor hemorrhage data?

options.A: Warning patients not to bleed too much after delivery
options.B: Fines for midwives who forget to chart the time of birth
options.C: Making practical changes like ready-to-use drug packs and staff drills
options.D: Hiding the data so the hospital reputation remains protected

explanation: Effective improvements fix the system workflow rather than just telling workers to try harder. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T4#BMP217_U2_T4_h5)

question: A maternity unit notices patients frequently complain about rude communication from night-shift staff. What is the most appropriate initial quality improvement response?

options.A: Fire all the night-shift midwives immediately without investigation
options.B: Lock the delivery unit doors so patients cannot leave feedback
options.C: Ignore the complaints because night shifts are naturally stressful
options.D: Organize supportive communication workshops and review shift handover routines

explanation: Addressing behavioral issues requires supportive training and looking at systemic factors like fatigue and shift stress. [learn more](BMP217_U2_T4#BMP217_U2_T4_h5)
